newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli CPI-linked bonds close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli CPI-linked bonds close sharply higher.

text.p: Israeli inflation-linked bonds closed sharply higher on Thursday following heavy trading by the provident funds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.04 pct to 102.18
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 101.38.
Volume was a high 240 million shekels with turnover in the Makams trading heavily for the second day running and accounting for 90 million shekels of the total.

"The bond market has made a very big move since the beginning of the year," said Yosi Levi of Ahrayut Investment Management. "CPI-linked-bonds continue to rise because the Bank of Israel is not issuing long bonds and provident funds have to buy them as they raise more money."
Traders noted that provident funds were the main buyers in the market.
"Yields on (CPI-linked) long bonds fell to 4.25 percent and I believe that they will continue falling untill they reach 4.0 percent," Levi added.

"Unlinked bonds and Makams are still rising but at a very slow pace," said a trader at Bank Leumi. "The Makam has gained 1.4 percent since the beginning of the year and the Gilon has risen 2.1 percent."
"Now they are expected to remain stable until the Bank of Israel decides on another rate cut," the trader added.
The central bank is not scheduled to change interest rates again until the end of February after lowering the base rate 0.5 percentage point to 14.2 percent effective today.
Traders said dollar-linked bonds closed lower following the overnight decline of the U.S. currency against the mark and yen in Asian markets.
In the local foreign currency market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3120 shekels unchanged from Wednesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
